name: librcsc
why: The RoboCup soccer simulation library behind the Helios team; a real multi-agent simulation you can run and watch.

brief.what_it_is: librcsc is a C++ library for building a simulated soccer team and related tools for the RoboCup Soccer Simulation (the 2D simulator). The README says all of its programs work with rcssserver-18, the simulation server. The Homebrew package installs the library plus a set of command-line tools: librcsc-config, librcscenv, rcg2csv, rcg2txt, rcgrenameteam, rcgresultprinter, rcgreverse, rcgvalidator, rcgverconv, rcgversion, rclmscheduler and rclmtableprinter. Judging by their names, the rcg* tools work on game log files (converting, validating, renaming teams, printing results) and the rclm* tools work on league data, but the README does not describe them individually.
brief.why_it_exists: The README presents it as a basic library for developing a simulated soccer team and related tools for the RoboCup Soccer Simulation. It is the foundation of the HELIOS Base team code, which the README cites as a related open-source package.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the internals of the library or the tools. It describes the build: an autotools workflow (bootstrap, configure, make, make install) that installs the library and headers under /usr/local by default or under a chosen --prefix. The README also cites two academic papers on HELIOS Base and the multi-agent positioning mechanism.

brief.install_notes: Requires C++17 and Boost 1.41 or later; Doxygen and Graphviz are optional. The README gives Ubuntu 20.04+ package commands. Installing under a home directory such as ~/local needs LD_LIBRARY_PATH set in ~/.bashrc and PATH set in ~/.profile, followed by logging out and back in. The README says configure defaults for helios-base, soccerwindow2 and fedit2 already expect ~/local. No accounts or hardware are needed. The Homebrew formula does not add caveats of its own.
brief.standout: It is the shared base library for a well-known open-source 2D soccer simulation team, and it ships a suite of log and league utilities alongside it. The README cites peer-reviewed papers on the team package.
brief.status: unknown. The README has no release date, version number, changelog or last-commit information, and I did not check the GitHub releases or commit history, so I cannot say whether it is actively maintained.
brief.caveats: The README does not mention Windows or macOS, so the build instructions are Linux-oriented, with apt-based package commands. Building from source needs autotools and Boost. The README says nothing about a viewer or a running simulation: the library and tools are the subject, and the simulator server (rcssserver) is a separate project. The scout note describes it as something you can run and watch, but I found no README support for that. Licence: LGPL v3 (per the badge in the README).
